req.title: Index shows post author name
req.statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-032 requires that the index page (GET /) renders the author's username alongside each post. The pre-loaded dataset has 20 posts authored by users Rahul (id=1), Anjali (id=2), Ishaan (id=3), Diya (id=4), and James (id=5). Tests must verify: (1) positive — known usernames appear in the HTML response body; (2) negative — a username that does NOT exist in the dataset is absent from the page; (3) boundary — the most-recent post (id=20, author Rahul) and the oldest post (id=8, author Rahul) both show the correct username, exercising the ORDER BY DESC boundary. Additional tests cover multiple distinct authors appearing simultaneously and exact HTTP status code. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes, exact byte strings, and both presence and absence of specific usernames.

tests.name: test_index_shows_known_author_username_positive
preconditions: Database contains pre-loaded 20 posts with authors Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, James
actions: Create in-process Flask app with temp database
Send GET / with test client
Inspect response body for known author usernames
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_shows_known_author_username_positive():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    os.unlink(path)

test_index_shows_known_author_username_positive()

tests.name: test_index_shows_multiple_distinct_authors_decision_table
preconditions: Database contains posts by at least three distinct authors: Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, James
Each author's username must appear in the rendered HTML
actions: Create in-process Flask app with temp database
Send GET / with test client
Assert each distinct author username present in response
Assert exact HTTP status code is 200 not 201 or 302
expected: b'Diya' NOT in response data (no posts)

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_shows_multiple_distinct_authors_decision_table():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200

    assert r.status_code != 302
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    assert b'Anjali' in r.data
    assert b'Ishaan' in r.data
    assert b'James' in r.data
    assert b'Diya' not in r.data

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_index_newly_created_post_shows_author_username_boundary():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    lr = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert lr.status_code == 302
    cr = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'BoundaryTestPost21', 'body': 'body text'})
    assert cr.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'BoundaryTestPost21' in r.data
    assert b'Rahul' in r.data
    os.unlink(path)
